An arranger keyboard turns one chord in your left hand into a band. Each **style** has eight channels (two rhythm,
bass, two chord, pad, two phrase), and each channel's pattern is written once, over a C major seventh chord. When you
hold a different chord, the keyboard moves every note of every pattern to fit it, using a rule set per channel. Press
Start (or turn on Sync Start and play a chord), then change chords and sections as you go.

## Channels

Each channel can be switched off, given another sound, or have its rules changed. The rules are what decide where the
notes go when the chord changes; open one to try them, and watch the score below change.

::: {#ar-mixer}
:::

## Score

Each channel of the section, drawn from the stored pattern. *As written* is what the style's author recorded over CM7;
*As it sounds* is the same pattern moved to the chord you hold.

::: {#ar-score}
:::

## How a style follows your chord

**Written over CM7.** Yamaha's style recording rules ask for every Main and Fill In pattern to be recorded over CM7: the
bass and phrase channels using only the notes of its scale (C D E G A B), the chord and pad channels only its chord tones
(C E G B). Every pattern on this page follows that rule, and a test checks it.

**Root: NTR.** *Root Trans* moves the whole pattern by the distance between the roots, so a line keeps its shape: C3 E3 G3
over F becomes F3 A3 C4. *High Key* stops it climbing forever: roots above it move down instead of up. *Root Fixed*
keeps notes near where they were written, so chords don't jump around: C3 E3 G3 over F becomes C3 F3 A3.

**Chord type: NTT.** *Melody* moves each scale note to the matching note of the new chord's scale (over a minor
seventh, E becomes E♭ and B becomes B♭). *Chord* moves each chord tone to the matching tone of the new chord. *Bypass*
changes nothing but the root; with Root Fixed it changes nothing at all, which is what the rhythm channels use. The minor
tables (Melodic, Harmonic, Natural Minor, Dorian) only switch between major and minor, lowering the 3rd and some of the
6th and 7th.

**Fingering.** *Fingered* reads the chord from all its notes. *Single Finger* builds it from one to three keys: one key
for major, the nearest black key to its left added for minor, the nearest white key for a seventh, both for a minor
seventh. *Multi Finger* takes either. *Fingered On Bass* uses your lowest key as the bass note, so C/E is possible.

**Sections.** The Intro plays first and leads into a Main. A Main repeats until you press another section; with Auto Fill
on, changing Main plays that Main's Fill In to the end of the bar first. Break is a one-bar gap; Ending plays out and stops.

**Unverified.** The manuals give the rules but not the exact tables, so the scale chosen for each chord type (Dorian over
minor sevenths, for instance), how Root Fixed picks its octave, the High Key default (F), and the exact moment fills and
endings start are this site's reading. The styles are this site's own patterns, not Yamaha's.
